correctness.rationale: After normalizing the base to height zero and the apex to \(hn\), the support function is the maximum of base and apex supports. If the projection \(p\) is outside \(B\), strict separation gives an explicit tilted direction of width below \(h\). If \(p\) is inside \(B\), every tilted direction reduces to \(rb+\max\{ra,h\sqrt{1-r^2}\}\). The branch switch occurs at \(r=h/\sqrt{h^2+a^2}\); concavity on the first branch and monotonicity on the second give the exact formula. Applying the condition to \(e\) and \(-e\) yields the symmetric iff criterion. The plank corollary then follows from the cited Corollary 7/Lemma 8 and exact pyramid homothety.

value.rationale: The recent partial-plank paper isolates higher-dimensional simplices with an altitude equal to minimum width but leaves that geometric hypothesis implicit. The formula makes the hypothesis exactly testable for every convex pyramid, identifies when a natural one-plank extremizer works in all dimensions, and also gives the minimum width itself whenever the apex projection lies in the base. This is a structural classification tied directly to an active plank-covering problem rather than an arbitrary slice or parameter increment.
